body:
>Was there a reason these were tied to physics tick?

There were some other artifacts like this that were fixed in recent versions of Godot that existed basically since it became open source, so it is hard to know what the original intention was (assuming it wasn't simply a mistake). The previous changes worked fine, so this should be a safe change too. 

See:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/87886
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98766

Tested locally (at various editor FPS), this makes scroll speed dependent on the *rendered* FPS. Scroll speed should be independent of both the physics FPS and the rendered FPS.

Both videos are recorded at 120 FPS but in the first one, the editor is rendering at 120 FPS while in the second one, it's rendering at 10 FPS by increasing **Low Processor Mode Sleep Usec** to `100000` then restarting the editor.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/456e5abe-bdb5-4b80-b209-414253aaabb2

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cf1b654-a87b-4510-a5e7-99a3f235e7b4

The lower your FPS, the slower it will scroll.

Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/215acd52e82f4c575abb715e25e54558deeef998), it works as expected. Varying FPS seem to work correctly now (tested with 10 FPS, 20 FPS, 30 FPS, 120 FPS and 1,000+ FPS).

A good improvement for a future PR would be to make smooth scrolling use ease-out transitions (and slow down the animation a bit to compensate). This way, it can feel more natural. This would also bring it closer to most other editors out there.
